class_evidence: Restricted to two-class time series (p.2; Sec. 3, p.3). 48 two-class apportions from 7 UCR datasets (Adiac, FaceAll, 50words, SLeaf, Wafer, Yoga, TwoPats), each a separate binary task (Sec. 4.2, pp.7-8, Table 1).
reduced_multiclass: Adiac (37 classes), FaceAll (14), 50words (50), SLeaf (15): one class positive, the rest merged as negative, one apportion per chosen class (Sec. 4.2, p.8).
smote_explanation: INOS splits the synthetic quota between two generators: 70% from ESPO, a regularised Gaussian of the minority covariance that does not interpolate (Sec. 3.2.2, Eq. 13; r = 0.7, Sec. 4.3), and 30% from ADASYN in a signal space with the null space removed (Sec. 3.3, Eqs. 14-15). The ADASYN part allocates points per seed by the share of negatives among its neighbours and interpolates uniformly towards one of the 5 nearest positives, as in SMOTE. Afterwards, Tomek-like noise links between synthetic positives and nearest negatives are removed (Sec. 3.4, pp.5-6).
corrections: Drop Placement rule (the interpolating part keeps uniform placement; ESPO is a separate generator); add Sample allocation and Post-filtering.
flags: ADASYN weighting could also count as Seed selection.

class_evidence: 4 artificial two-class domains (Sec. 5.3, pp.11-12) and 20 UCI datasets used as two-class problems (Sec. 5.4, p.13, Table 5); networks with 2 output neurons (Sec. 5.2). Multiclass use named as future work (Sec. 6, p.19).
reduced_multiclass: Multiclass sources converted to two-class problems with the chosen minority and majority classes listed in Table 5 (Sec. 5.4, p.13); the table could not be extracted from the text.
smote_explanation: Seeds are limited to an informative minority set near the borderline majority points, after dropping minority points whose neighbours are all majority (Alg. 1 steps 1-6; Sec. 4.1, p.5). Each seed gets a weight from its closeness to the majority class and its density, and seeds are drawn in proportion to it, so counts per seed vary (Alg. 1 steps 7-9, 12a; Sec. 4.2, pp.6-7). The partner is a random member of the seed's minority cluster from average-linkage clustering, not one of its 5 nearest neighbours (Alg. 1 steps 10, 12b; Secs. 4.3-4.4). Placement is uniform on the segment and nothing is removed afterwards.
corrections: Add Sample allocation (weighted seed draws give unequal counts per seed).
flags: Exact class mapping in Table 5 not checked.

class_evidence: Two-class: 4 synthetic 2-D sets (Sec. 4.3.1, p.406) and 27 UCI sets used as binary (Table 2, p.409), each at 0-30% label noise. Multiclass: 8 UCI sets with all classes kept, 3 to 5 classes (Table 7, p.416; Sec. 4.3.3, pp.413-414), macro-averaged metrics (Eqs. 7-10, p.405). Same generator in both.
reduced_multiclass: Several of the 27 binary sets come from multiclass UCI sources (e.g. ecoli, iris, wine, segment, vehicle; Table 2, p.409); the reduction is not described but counts suggest one class vs the rest.
multiclass_how: Every class smaller than the largest is oversampled with RSMOTE up to the largest class size (Sec. 4.3.3, p.413); classification uses diversified one-against-one classifiers (p.414).
smote_explanation: Minority points whose k neighbours are all majority are dropped as noise, and the remaining seeds are split into borderline and safe groups by 2-means on their relative density (Defs. 1-3, pp.401-402; Algorithm 1, p.403). Each group gets a share matching its size, and within a group each seed gets a weight (k-m)/(k+1), so safer seeds produce more points (Step 3, p.402). Points are made with SMOTE's own routine, uniform on the segment, once before training (Algorithm 1 line 22).
flags: Whether partners are limited to the seed's own group is not specified.

class_evidence: Defined for labels {-1,+1} (Sec. 3.3, p.5). 42 two-class datasets: 30 low-dimensional UCI/KEEL and 12 high-dimensional microarray sets (Table 1, p.7; Sec. 4.1, pp.6-7); binary AUC and G-mean.
reduced_multiclass: Low-dimensional sets are mostly KEEL 'x vs y' and one-vs-rest versions of multiclass sources (Table 1, p.7); the paper does not describe the reduction.
smote_explanation: The only change is how the k nearest minority neighbours are found: Euclidean distance is replaced by a feature-weighted Minkowski distance whose weights come from a supervised feature ranking, and low-ranked features can be dropped from the distance (Eqs. 4-5, 9-12, pp.4-5; Algorithm 1 steps 2-9). Seeds, the number per seed, the random partner and placement on the segment are as in SMOTE (Algorithm 1 steps 10-14), and the method reduces to SMOTE with equal weights and p = 2 (p.6).

class_evidence: 21 UCI datasets, all multiclass (Abstract; Sec. IV-A-1, p.5; Table 1), all classes kept and scored with multiclass MG and MAUC (Eqs. 6-7, p.6); 5-fold CV, CART and SVM. No two-class experiment.
multiclass_how: Every class with N_max/N_i > 1.45 is oversampled towards the largest class size, each class independently, with the neighbour search over all classes (Alg. 1; Sec. III, pp.4-5). No decomposition.
smote_explanation: A minority point is a seed only if at least half of its 5 nearest neighbours, taken from all classes, share its class (Sec. III step 2; Alg. 1). Instead of a random minority partner, the method uses the centroid of the seed's neighbours and places new points on the line from that centroid through the seed, possibly beyond the seed (Sec. III steps 3-5; Alg. 1 lines 23-26). It generates twice the needed number and keeps the candidates nearest the centroid (Sec. III step 6, p.5).
corrections: Add Neighbour choice (kNN centroid replaces the random partner) and Post-filtering (over-generation and removal of far candidates).
flags: Per-dataset class counts in Table 1 could not be extracted.

class_evidence: 20 datasets (Sec. 4.1, Table 1, pp.6-7): 14 KEEL multiclass sets with all classes kept (3 to 10 classes, e.g. car, glass, yeast, zoo) and 6 two-class software-defect sets (camel-1.4, camel-1.6, hive-0.12.0, velocity-1.5, xalan-2.4, xerces-1.2). All three variants run on all 20 sets (Tables 5-8, pp.10-11).
reduced_multiclass: None; the defect sets are natively two-class.
multiclass_how: Mean class size m is the target (Eq. 1): classes below m are oversampled up to m, classes above m are cleaned by one of three strategies (Sec. 3.2, pp.5-6). No decomposition.
smote_explanation: Generation interpolates between a minority seed and one of its 5 same-class neighbours (Eq. 3, p.3), but each seed-direction pair gets a weight that favours safe seeds (same-class share among neighbours, Eq. 2) and directions whose synthetic region holds few other-class points (Eqs. 5-10). Each minority class is filled to the mean class size by weighted random draws rather than a fixed number per seed (Alg. 1). Afterwards, original majority points in the synthetic regions, or overlapping other majority classes, are removed (Sec. 3.2, Eqs. 11-16).
corrections: Add Seed selection (safe factor weights seeds).
flags: Eq. 3 draws a random value per feature, so points fill the box between seed and neighbour rather than the segment; the paper presents this as SMOTE. Only original majority points are filtered.
